newsitem.title: USA: Bridgeport, Conn, plans $50 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: Bridgeport, Conn, plans $50 mln bond sale.

text.p: Bridgeport, Connecticut plans to competitively sell as much as $50 million of general obligation bonds in the next 30 days for capital improvements, said Mayor Joseph Ganim on Wednesday.
The mayor added that the city expects to sell up to $30 million of additional bonds in the next nine to 12 months, depending on when the various projects are ready.

The mayor added that the city, whose yearly budget totals about $340 million, had not yet decided whether it would sell any more bonds this year. "I don't know. Those are the only ones we're ready to sell in the near future," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Bridgeport does not plan to sell bonds to finance approximately $250 million to $260 million of unfunded pension liabilities. "We're not doing any bonds with regard to pensions," Ganim said.

His spokesman noted that the city, Connecticut's largest with about 140,000 residents, has not had problems meeting this obligation, and the plan has been closed since 1984. Police and firefighters hired since then have joined a separate plan that is fully funded, said Christopher Duby, the mayor's spokesman.

The city, located on the Long Island Sound about 20 miles southwest of New Haven, expects to finalize its next fiscal budget in May. The Mayor said his plan likely will include only a minimal increase, if any, in overall spending, and seek to trim discretionary spending while finding funds for 80 more police officers as well as another tax cut, which would be its second in a row.
